title: Sparse session-stitched serializer — scratch notes
content:
Goal: sketch a compact, forward-compatible on-disk/transfer format for sessions that can be partially stitched back together across workers/tenants. This is a working brain-dump — lots of TODOs and heuristics.

Motivation / constraints:
- We need a format to offload idle sessions from GPU memory (KV) to cheaper storage and later rehydrate without losing the ability to cheaply resume generation.
- Many sessions are sparse (long chat with a few active topics) — storing full token streams is wasteful. We want delta + anchors + sparse checkpoints.
- Support cross-worker handoff and partial reads: e.g., a local edge runner wants tokens 0..N and last-k KV; a dedicated worker wants full KV to resume low-latency.
- Security: stored blobs may be customer-sensitive. Must play nicely with KMS-wrapped encryption, but format should support both encrypted and plaintext variants for internal debugging.
- Forward compatibility: runtime may evolve (new cache slots, extra metadata). Keep simple versioning and field tags.

Design primitives (v0 sketch):
1) Manifest (small JSON header; always unencrypted when wrapped)
   - version: int (start 1)
   - session_id: string
   - owner_tenant: string
   - model: string (short id)
   - created_at / last_active_at timestamps
   - anchors: list of anchor descriptors (see below)
   - segments: index of binary segments by name + compressed size + sha256
   - flags: e.g., encrypted=true|false, partial_allowed=true|false

2) Anchors (sparse reference points)
   - anchor_id: short id
   - seq_range: [start_token_index, end_token_index] (end exclusive)
   - kv_snapshot_refs: list of segment names that contain KV slices for this range
   - priority: hot|warm|cold (used by prefetch heuristics)
   - tags: freeform (e.g., "system-instruction-boundary")

3) Binary segments (opaque blobs, individually compressible & encryptable)
   - token_deltas: compressed token diffs (relative offsets) OR compact transcript slices (utf-8)
   - kv_shards: contiguous ranges of KV cache (layer, head, chunk offsets) – format: layer:int; start_idx:int; length:int; bytes: base64||raw
   - attachment_blobs: small derived artifacts (index vectors, canonicalized prompts)

Why segments: allow partial fetch and checksum validation. Workers can request only the segments referenced by an anchor. Also allows dedup across sessions (shared embeddings, repeated prompts).

Delta encoding ideas:
- Store canonical tokens once, then deltas as edits/insertions referencing canonical positions. This suits long-running conversations where repeated few tokens change (low churn).
- Simpler fallback: store sequential token slices with run-length encoding for repeated system messages.

APIs (sketch):
- POST /session/serialize
   Body: { session_id, want_level: [full|anchor-only|metadata], anchors: [anchor_ids]? , encrypt:kms_key_id? }
   Response: { manifest_id, manifest_blob (JSON), presigned_segments: [{name, url, range?}] }
   Notes: if encrypt provided, server returns manifest with encryption metadata. Presigned URLs are short lived.

- GET /session/manifest/{manifest_id}
   Response: manifest JSON (same shape as stored header)

- GET /session/segment/{manifest_id}/{segment_name}
   Query: range (optional)
   Response: raw blob (possibly encrypted)

- POST /session/rehydrate
   Body: { manifest_id, wanted_anchor_id?, read_hints: ["last-k-kv", "full-kv", "token-range:100-200"], prefer_local_cache:true|false }
   Response: { status, rehydration_ticket: ephemeral_id, node_assigned }
   Notes: rehydrate kicks background prefetch; ticket used for subsequent /session/resume-call with affinity.

Heuristics for anchors / what to persist:
- Hotness score = f(last_active_ms, tokens_since_last_user_message, explicit_user_attention)
- Only persist anchors when hotness falls below threshold OR memory pressure forces eviction. Anchors have different retention policies (hot=fast restore, cold=cheap store).
- Prefer to snapshot end-of-turn (user message boundary) anchors. Easier to resume without recomputing state.
- For long-term cold storage, strip KV entirely and keep token deltas + model+temperature metadata (useful for offline auditing).

Prefetch strategies:
- Client hints: client may include desired latency/price tradeoff in rehydrate request (e.g., "cold-resume-cost-limit": 0.02) which routes to different prefetch plans.
- Progressive warmup: fetch smallest prioritized segments first (last layer KV + recent tokens) so generation can start while rest warms in background.
- Probabilistic fetch: if user likely to ask about a past topic (based on topic-marker tags), prefetch related anchors.

Stitching across workers (hand-off):
- Two-stage: source worker serializes manifest + segments; target worker pulls manifest; target requests segments it needs; after verification target calls /session/confirm-handoff which does a CAS on manifest ETag to ensure no concurrent writes.
- If concurrent updates: manifest version conflict -> require merge policy (last-write-wins OR operational transform on token_deltas).

Compatibility + versioning:
- Manifest version increments on any structural change. Segments are opaque with content-type tags.
- Schema evolution rules: unknown fields ignored; new required fields must have default semantics.

Security notes:
- Always support KMS-wrapped symmetric encryption per-tenant. Manifest header should contain minimal metadata unencrypted.
- Audit trail: store manifest changes as append-only log (link to current manifest).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Binary format for kv_shards: protobuf? custom packed array? Must optimize for sequential reads for contiguous layer slices.
- How to represent cross-model shared embeddings? Dedup references? content-addressed segment pool?
- Garbage collection: how to safely delete shared segments referenced by multiple manifests (refcount store?).
- Cost model for prefetch (how many tokens / bytes to fetch for a given latency SLO). Need simulated workload + traces.
- Granularity tradeoffs: many tiny segments makes prefetch chatty; few huge segments wastes bandwidth. Need heuristics tuned per workload.

Quick sketch of an example manifest (human readable):
{
  "version": 1,
  "session_id": "sess::abcd-1234",
  "model": "redwood-rlhf-1.3",
  "anchors": [
    {"anchor_id":"A0","seq_range":[0,128],"kv_snapshot_refs":["kv-l0-0-32"],"priority":"cold"},
    {"anchor_id":"A1","seq_range":[128,256],"kv_snapshot_refs":["kv-l0-32-64","kv-l1-0-32"],"priority":"hot"}
  ],
  "segments": {"tokens-A1":"s3://.../seg-123","kv-l0-32-64":"s3://.../seg-456"},
  "flags": {"encrypted":true,"partial_allowed":true}
}

Notes to self:
- Implement small prototype: pack kv_shard as (layer:int32, start:int32, length:int32, bytes) in little-endian, gzip. Wrap with content-type tag.
- Add a unit test that simulates progressive warmup (start with last-layer kv + recent tokens) and measure responses-start-time.
- Check overlap with Confluence RFC v2 (linked) and try to reconcile anchor naming.

Slack crumbs: convo #runtime-serializers 2024-10-16 (Ethan) about using content-addressed pool. Follow up on storage refcount approach.

Delivery plan (quick):
- Week 0-2: prototype pack/unpack and REST API (mock storage).
- Week 3-4: add KMS integration and progressive warmup test harness.
- Week 5: run replay on 72h production trace and tune anchor heuristics.

If anyone picks this up: ping me (Priya) and start with the proto pack/unpack code in serving-runtime/utils/session_store. Keep thing minimal and iteratively grow.

End of scratch notes.
